domes.name: 1V geodesic dome (a.k.a. 2/3)
domes.notes: 1V calculator page (https://www.domerama.com/calculators/1v-geodesic-dome-calculator/) labels this dome '1V (a.k.a 2/3)' and gives the same strut count (25 x A) and angle (31.72 deg) but does not show the chord factor decimal; chord factor 1.05146 comes only from the chord-charts page. 15 3-sided faces per chord-charts page.

domes.name: 2V geodesic dome
domes.notes: LETTER MISMATCH BETWEEN PAGES: the 2V calculator page (https://www.domerama.com/calculators/2v-geodesic-dome-calculator/) lists '30 X A' at 15.86 deg and '35 X B' at 18 deg -- i.e. its A/B labels are swapped relative to the chord-charts page. Struts above are matched to chord factors by angle (18deg->CF .61803 count 35; 15.86deg->CF .54653 count 30), using chord-charts' own lettering. Verify against the live site before treating letters as authoritative. 40 3-sided faces per chord-charts page. Hub counts (10x6-way,6x5-way,10x4-way) and bolt counts (26 bolts/26 nuts/52 washers) are from the calculator page.

domes.name: 3V 3/8 geodesic dome
domes.notes: Strut counts/angles/letters match the dedicated 3V 3/8 calculator page exactly (120 struts total). Chord factors from chord-charts page (https://www.domerama.com/calculators/chord-charts/), whose single '3V' table (30A/40B/50C) is this 3/8 truncation. Bolted assembly: 46 bolts/46 nuts/92 washers. Base is NOT flat (odd-frequency Class I dome); see Kruschke variant for flat-base version.

domes.name: 3V 5/8 geodesic dome
domes.notes: This is the default/main 3V calculator page on the site. Strut letters and angles (A@10.04, B@11.64, C@11.90) are identical to the 3/8 variant, only counts differ (165 struts total), so the same 3 chord factors from the chord-charts page apply -- confirmed by exact angle match, not independently published as a separate '5/8' chord factor table on site. Bolted assembly: 61 bolts/61 nuts/122 washers. Base is NOT flat (odd-frequency Class I dome).

domes.name: 3V 4/9 Flat Base Kruschke
domes.notes: URL slug and page title call this '3V 3/8' / '3v-38', but the on-page truncation label is '4/9'. Per the site's own 'Leveling the base of a dome' page, builders commonly call the Kruschke 4/9 dome '3/8' and the Kruschke 5/9 dome '5/8' -- legacy terminology, not the same fraction as the non-Kruschke Method-1 3/8 and 5/8 domes above. No chord factor decimals are shown anywhere on this page or in its page source/JS -- only bend angles. 4 strut types (A-D), 120 struts total, vs 3 strut types for the standard (non-Kruschke) 3/8 dome -- this matches the site's explicit statement that Kruschke domes need one extra strut length to achieve a flat base. Bolted assembly: 46 bolts/46 nuts/92 washers.

domes.name: 3V 5/9 Flat Base Kruschke

domes.name: 4V 1/2 geodesic dome (Method 1, chord-charts table)
domes.notes: AMBIGUOUS -- counts NOT reliably assignable. The chord-charts page (https://www.domerama.com/calculators/chord-charts/) gives 6 chord factors for '4V 1/2 method 1' but its own strut listing does not give per-letter counts, only '160 3-sided faces' for the whole table. The separate 4V calculator page (https://www.domerama.com/calculators/4v-geodesic-dome-calculator/) gives counts (30A@7.27,30B@8.49,60C@8.47,70D@9.35,30E@8.59,30F@9.00 = 250 struts) but its angles do not line up cleanly with the chord-charts angles: chord-charts has TWO different chord factors sharing angle 9.35 deg (C=.29453 and F=.29859) while the calculator page has only ONE strut type at 9.35 deg (D, count 70); the calculator page's B is 8.49 deg vs chord-charts' B at 8.47 deg (likely a typo on one page, cause unknown). We deliberately did NOT force a letter-for-letter or count assignment here since that would be inventing data. See the next entry for the calculator page's own raw counts. Recommend independently re-deriving these 6 chord factors geometrically for the Blender plugin's pass/fail set rather than trusting the site's count-to-CF pairing for 4V.

domes.name: Octahedral 5V, Mexican method (1/2)
domes.method: Mexican method (equal-central-path triangulation, Hector Alfredo Hernandez Hernandez)
domes.notes: NOT a Kruschke dome -- a separate, distinct alternate method. Site: The so-called Mexican Method is named after the work of Mexican mathematician Hector Alfredo Hernandez Hernandez. With this system of triangle subdivision, strut lengths are equalized along each set of three paths followed by the struts. As a result, the number of unique strut lengths equals the dome's frequency (5 types for 5V). The method can be applied to geodesic domes based on either the octahedron or icosahedron, but the equal-length feature begins to break down at frequency 6. Base polyhedron here is OCTAHEDRON, not icosahedron. No chord factor decimals published, angle only. 160 struts total.
